notes: entry_point is the single declared location for how the runner is invoked.
It is 'console-script' as of runner_ref 600744a5, which fixed the broken
gen_eval.__main__:main entry point (UPSTREAM.md UP-1).
schemas_upstream_published is true: gen-eval now ships versioned JSON Schema in
gen_eval.contracts (UP-2), so the vendored copies under
openspec/contracts/cli-gen-eval/ are verbatim copies of the published files plus
provenance annotations — not derived or hand-assembled here.
contract_version must equal gen_eval.contracts.CONTRACT_VERSION; the generator
refuses to write when they disagree.
runner_limits are OBSERVED properties of the pinned runner, not settings. None is
exposed on its CLI. max_expansions_per_template caps one template's parameter
expansion. max_scenarios_per_iteration truncates the generated list; the
orchestrator then buckets what survives and gives int(total*tier_changed_share) to
scenarios matching --changed-features-ref, int(total*tier_critical_share) to
priority <= critical_priority_max, and the remainder to everything else. The
change-detection tier does NOT reflow when unused, so a run without a change ref
can evaluate only critical+remainder = 30 of a nominal 50, at most 13 of which may
be non-critical. Every one of these drops work with a log warning and exit 0, which
is why they are recorded here and asserted against the checked-in suite in
tests/cli_gen_eval/test_descriptor_drift.py. Re-verify them when bumping
runner_ref; raised upstream as UPSTREAM.md UP-6.
runner_source is a git ref only as an interim measure. Repointing it at an
artifact index is a change to this file alone.
